skill.name: fp-ts-react
skill.description: Provides practical fp-ts patterns for React hooks, state, forms, data fetching, dependency injection, testing, and React 19 features.
skill.summary: Build predictable React applications with type-safe functional programming patterns.

security_audit.summary: All 85 static findings are false positives in Markdown documentation and TypeScript examples. Backticks format code or form template literals, while fetch calls use illustrative relative endpoints. No prompt injection, secret access, obfuscation, reconnaissance, or hidden command behavior was found.

static_findings.snippet: | `Option` | Value might be missing (user not loaded yet) |
Use `Option` instead of `null | undefined` for clearer intent.
Either is perfect for validation: `Left` = errors, `Right` = valid data.
Stop using `{ data, loading, error }` booleans. Use a proper state machine.
fp-ts values like `O.some(1)` create new objects each render. React sees them as "changed".
| Form with multiple validations | `Either` with validation applicative |
Either is perfect for validation: `Left` = errors, `Right` = valid data.

content.user_title: Build Type-Safe React Apps with fp-ts
content.value_statement: React async state and validation often become inconsistent. This skill provides fp-ts patterns for predictable hooks, forms, data fetching, and dependency injection.
actual_capabilities: Models optional React state with Option and explicit fallback handling.
Builds form validation with Either, including accumulated and field-level errors.
Wraps asynchronous requests in TaskEither and composes sequential or parallel operations.
Represents loading, failure, and success with a RemoteData state machine.
Improves referential stability with useMemo and equality-aware hooks.
Structures dependency injection, mock services, and React 19 form patterns.
limitations: Examples require adaptation to project types, APIs, and error models.
The skill does not install dependencies or execute the documented code.
Runtime response validation needs an additional library such as io-ts or Zod.
React and fp-ts version compatibility still requires project-level testing.

use_cases.title: Model Predictable UI State
use_cases.description: Replace nullable values and conflicting loading flags with Option and RemoteData.

use_cases.title: Validate Complex Forms
use_cases.description: Accumulate field errors and preserve typed success values with Either.

use_cases.title: Design Testable Service Access
use_cases.description: Inject API and analytics services through context and verify components with mocks.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Nullable State
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this React state from null handling to fp-ts Option and explain each match branch.

prompt_templates.title: Build Form Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create typed Either validators for these fields and return every validation error at once.

prompt_templates.title: Compose API Requests
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor these dependent and parallel requests with TaskEither, preserving typed errors and loading states.

prompt_templates.title: Architect Functional Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Design ReaderTaskEither dependencies, React context wiring, RemoteData rendering, and mock-based tests for this feature.

output_examples.input: Model a profile that may be absent and render a login fallback.
output_examples.output: An Option-based state design with explicit absent and present render paths, plus a short explanation of the transitions.

output_examples.input: Validate signup fields and show all problems together.
output: Typed validators for name, email, and password.
An accumulated error model for simultaneous feedback.
A React submission flow that handles failure and success.

output_examples.input: Load dashboard resources concurrently with typed failures.
output_examples.output: A TaskEither composition plan covering parallel requests, combined success data, failure mapping, and RemoteData rendering.

best_practices: Keep domain errors typed and map them to user messages near the interface.
Memoize constructed fp-ts values when React dependency identity matters.
Test every tagged state and both branches of Option or Either.
anti_patterns: Do not combine independent loading, data, and error flags that permit impossible states.
Do not recreate Option values each render when effects depend on reference identity.
Do not cast unvalidated network responses directly into trusted domain types.

faq.question: Which React versions are covered?
faq.answer: The examples cover React 18 and React 19, with notes relevant to Next.js 14 and 15.

faq.question: Does this skill install fp-ts?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples, while dependency installation remains a project decision.

faq.question: Can it collect multiple form errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It demonstrates applicative validation and field-level error structures.

faq.question: Does TaskEither validate response data?
faq.answer: No. Add runtime validation with io-ts, Zod, or another schema library.

faq.question: How does it prevent invalid async states?
faq.answer: It models not-started, loading, failure, and success as distinct RemoteData variants.

faq.question: Can these patterns be tested?
faq.answer: Yes. The dependency injection section demonstrates context providers and mock services for component tests.
